method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Check a BGL in most acutely unwell children** — diabetes can present non-specifically.
claims.source_text: A blood glucose level (BGL) should be checked in most acutely unwell children, as diabetes can present non-specifically
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnostic: random BGL 11.1 mmol/L or more, or fasting BGL 7.0 mmol/L or more, together with symptoms of hyperglycaemia.**
claims.source_text: Random BGL ≥11.1 mmol/L or fasting BGL ≥7.0 mmol/L, together with symptoms of hyperglycaemia, are diagnostic of diabetes in a child
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Classic symptoms:** polydipsia, polyuria, new nocturnal enuresis in a previously dry child, unexplained weight loss or fatigue. Vomiting, respiratory distress, dehydration, abdominal pain or altered consciousness may indicate ketosis/ketoacidosis.
claims.source_text: polydipsia (excessive thirst) polyuria (excessive urination) new onset nocturnal enuresis (ie in a child who was previously dry overnight) unexplained weight loss unexplained fatigue … Other non-specific presentations (which may indicate ketosis/ketoacidosis) include vomiting, respiratory distress, dehydration, abdominal pain, altered consciousness
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not diagnose on a single BGL without symptoms**; if in doubt, HbA1c, OGTT or continued BGL monitoring with a paediatric specialist.
claims.source_text: A diagnosis of diabetes should not be based on a single BGL reading in the absence of symptoms of hyperglycaemia. If the diagnosis is in doubt additional testing may be required (eg HbA1c, OGTT, continued monitoring of BGLs)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most childhood diabetes is type 1.** If autoantibodies are negative, consider **type 2** (obesity, acanthosis nigricans, strong family history) or **monogenic** diabetes (presentation under 6 months, or autosomal dominant family history).
claims.source_text: Most cases of diabetes in children are due to Type 1 diabetes mellitus … Type 2 diabetes: obesity, acanthosis nigricans, strong family history Monogenic diabetes: <6 months of age at presentation (neonatal diabetes mellitus), autosomal dominant family history of diabetes (MODY)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Formal serum glucose; point-of-care blood ketones if random BGL is 11.1 mmol/L or more** (urine ketones if blood ketones are unavailable); venous blood gas.
claims.source_text: Formal serum blood glucose level Point of care blood ketones if random BGL ≥11.1 mmol/L urine ketones may be used for initial assessment if blood ketones are unavailable Venous blood gas
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **pH under 7.3 or bicarbonate under 18 mmol/L: manage as DKA.**
claims.source_text: If pH <7.3 or bicarbonate <18 mmol/L, manage as per Diabetic ketoacidosis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also send:** UEC, diabetes autoantibodies (anti-GAD, IAA, anti-IA2, ZnT8), coeliac serology, TSH and FT4.
claims.source_text: UEC Diabetes autoantibodies: anti-GAD, insulin autoantibodies (IAA), insulinoma-associated-2 autoantibodies (anti-IA2), zinc transporter 8 (ZnT8) Coeliac serology (transglutaminase IgA and total IgA) TSH, FT4
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A child not in DKA can be managed with subcutaneous insulin.** ⚠️ **If ketones are 0.6 or more, start insulin as soon as possible to prevent DKA.**
claims.source_text: A child with a new diagnosis of diabetes mellitus who is not in DKA can be managed with subcutaneous insulin injections … If ketones are elevated (≥0.6) insulin should be started as soon as possible to prevent DKA
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Initial total daily dose (TDD):** under 1 year — consult a paediatric endocrinologist · 1–5 years 0.5 units/kg/day · 5–10 years 0.7 units/kg/day · over 10 years 0.7–1.0 units/kg/day.
claims.source_text: Initial total daily dose (TDD) For children <1 year consult paediatric endocrinologist 1-5 years: 0.5 units/kg/day 5-10 years: 0.7 units/kg/day >10 years: 0.7-1.0 units/kg/day
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **MDI (basal-bolus): 40% of TDD as long-acting insulin in the evening; the other 60% as rapid-acting split across breakfast, lunch and dinner** (~0.1–0.2 units/kg before each main meal).
claims.source_text: MDI insulin dosing (also called basal-bolus insulin) … Give 40% of TDD as long-acting insulin in the evening Divide remaining 60% into 3 doses of rapid-acting insulin and give pre-meal at breakfast, lunch and dinner ie ~0.1 - 0.2 units/kg before each main meal
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First rapid-acting dose more than 2 hours before a meal: consider a stat 0.2 units/kg.** Daytime presenters may need slightly higher pre-meal doses (e.g. 0.25 units/kg) until the evening basal dose. **Round doses down to the nearest 0.5 unit.**
claims.source_text: If commencing first dose rapid-acting insulin >2 hours before mealtime, consider giving stat 0.2 units/kg of insulin; then begin regular rapid-acting insulin with meals as above Children presenting during the day may need slightly higher pre-meal doses (eg 0.25 units/kg) until basal insulin is given that evening Round insulin dose down to nearest 0.5 unit
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pre-meal target 4–8 mmol/L.** Above 8, use the correction factor to bring BGL back to 6 mmol/L, unless insulin was given in the preceding 2 hours. **Give pre-meal rapid-acting insulin 15 minutes before the meal** (Fiasp at the time of the meal).
claims.source_text: Pre-meal BGL target is 4-8 mmol/L. If BGL >8 mmol/L use CF to determine dose of rapid-acting insulin to return BGL to 6 mmol/L (unless insulin has already been given in preceding 2 hours) Pre-meal rapid-acting insulin should be given 15 minutes prior to the meal (except Fiasp®, which can be given at the time of the meal due to faster onset)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Flexible dosing: rapid-acting dose = (BGL − 6) ÷ correction factor, plus carbohydrate grams ÷ insulin:carbohydrate ratio.** Also give with snacks over 15 g carbohydrate.
claims.source_text: Flexible insulin dosing: The dose of rapid-acting insulin is calculated before each meal (or snack) based on pre-meal BGL and the amount of carbohydrates being consumed … Insulin dose = 1) Insulin needed to correct BGL (child's BGL minus target BGL 6 mmol/L, then divide by correction factor) plus 2) Insulin needed to cover carbohydrate being eaten (grams of carbohydrate divided by insulin:carbohydrate ratio) … with snacks containing >15 grams of carbohydrate
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Worked example:** pre-lunch BGL 16, eating 20 g carbohydrate, CF 2, ICR 5 → (16 − 6) = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 units, plus 20 ÷ 5 = 4 units → **9 units**. Not eating or under 15 g carbohydrate: correction only. BGL 4–8 with food: carbohydrate dose only.
claims.source_text: eg pre-lunch BGL 16, eating 20 g carb, child has CF 2 and ICR 5 … 16 (child's BGL) - 6 (target BGL) = 10 mmol/L 10 mmol/L ÷ 2 (CF) = 5 units 2) Insulin to cover carbohydrates being eaten (ICR) = 20 grams ÷ 5 (ICR) = 4 units 3) Give insulin 5 + 4 = 9 units … If giving insulin to correct BGL but child is not eating or eating <15 grams carbohydrate, calculate insulin dose using CF only ie step 1 only If giving insulin with food and BGL 4-8 mmol/L, use step 2 only
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Twice-daily injections are rarely used** as a standard regimen. Individualise doses and discuss ongoing dosing with a paediatric endocrinologist or experienced paediatrician.
claims.source_text: twice daily (BD dosing) injections are rarely used as a standard regimen … Where possible, discuss ongoing insulin dosing with a paediatric endocrinologist or paediatrician with experience in paediatric diabetes and always consult local guidelines where available
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **MDI finger-prick BGLs:** pre-meals, 2 am during initial stabilisation, and whenever hypoglycaemia is suspected; more often initially (e.g. 2 hours after the first dose and 4-hourly overnight), especially if ketotic.
claims.source_text: Multiple daily injections (MDI) … Pre-meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) 2 am (during initial stabilisation/admission) Whenever hypoglycaemia is suspected Note: more frequent BGL monitoring may be required on initial administration eg 2 hours following first insulin dose and 4-hourly overnight, especially if child is ketotic
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ketones present at diagnosis: measure with each BGL every 2 hours until under 0.6.** Thereafter check ketones whenever BGL is 15 or more or the child is unwell.
claims.source_text: If ketones are present at diagnosis, continue to measure with each BGL every 2 hours until ketones <0.6 … As part of ongoing management, ketones should be checked whenever BGL ≥15 or child is unwell
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss every new presentation with the local paediatric team; most are admitted** for insulin initiation and education. HITH/ambulatory programs only after discussion with paediatric endocrinology.
claims.source_text: For all new presentations of diabetes in children. In most centres these children need to be admitted for initiation of insulin therapy and diabetes education … In some tertiary centres, hospital in the home (HITH)/ambulatory care programs may be considered in appropriate cases; discuss with paediatric endocrinology team first
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** tolerating oral intake, linked with the local diabetes team, initial education done, and the family is competent with BGL monitoring, insulin and hypoglycaemia treatment.
claims.source_text: Child tolerating oral intake Child linked in with local diabetes care team and contact information provided Initial diabetes education completed, usually involves input from diabetes nurse educator, dietician, social work Family competent in monitoring BGLs and administering insulin and treating hypoglycaemia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_Mellitus__new_presentation/, retrieved 2026-09-23
